reviews.review:
I can't recommend this game in its current state, really.

It's the good foundation for a game, but it's not much beyond that. It feels janky in all the worst ways that a horde shooter can, primarily in the 'just-okay' gunplay, weak enemy feedback in terms of death animations and hit sounds, and overall floatiness. Enemies don't feel like they inhabit the world that you're tromping through, and instead it's painfully obvious that they're just gameplay assets plopped into a map. The characters in the game are pretty damned plain, too.

Contrast with something like Vermintide 2, where the impact of the melee combat feels amazing, and you never stop to think about how the enemies exist in the world. They stumble around, react to your hits, vault over obstacles in polished ways, they flow like a river that crashes against you and they make the game feel alive and very rarely make you think about the AI. The same is true about something like Deep Rock Galactic, which rewards you with satisfying and heavy-feeling gunplay, meaty hit-sounds when your bullets impact enemies and excellently rewarding death sounds. The way bugs 'pop' when they die in DRG makes every kill feel great, and when they hit YOU it makes sense and looks right. They move and behave naturally no matter what environment they're in.

But in Anacrusis, it's painfully obvious that the enemies are video game objects placed into a map. You'll notice all manner of weird AI behaviors and floatiness in their animations. Their attacks never look like they connect with you or anyone else, they just kind of stand near you and swing their arms at the air and you take damage. They're just not polished, and as a consequence they're really boring to fight. The best comparison I can make is almost like plonking enemies into a GMod map; their AI will do its best, but they're completely disconnected from the environments they're in and that much will be really obvious.

Also, their animations are really canned and pretty stiff. Everything about them is boring; the way they move, their attack animations, even the way they die. At best they just flop over dead with no gore effects and no specific reactions to the way you hit them, and at worst they pop into the air because something about their physics bugs out... although that's more fun to watch, tbh. The lifeblood of a good horde shooter is... well, a good horde, and the Anacrusis is severely lacking this in basically every way possible. 

All of this ends in a game that feels... kind of cheap. It's stuff that can be fixed in EA, thank goodness, but it's not really worth playing in its current state, especially not for $30. There's other horde shooters you could play that cost just as much if not less, and do everything that this game does but better. On the one hand, the problems that this game faces are the exact reason you would want to launch into Early Access, but usually an EA title has to launch with something specific really polished and ready to go, so that you have some reason to play it; something to hook players in, and keep them invested while everything else gets polished. Not so for the Anacrusis, which has nothing really going for it.

So, while I have hope that this game will improve, you should really wait, because right now it's nothing special. And, honestly, while Early Access can promise more improvements, the game needs to improve severely in polish all across the board, and I don't know if I'm confident that they'll be able to address every single problem with it and completely overhaul the zombies to be more interesting enemies than they are now. Sometimes even small things can make a game amazing, but core gameplay stuff left unpolished can also completely ruin a game.

Deep Rock Galactic wouldn't be half as fun as it is if you didn't get those amazing hit-sounds when landing bullets on a bug, or if the bugs didn't 'pop' when they die the way that they do. These little touches of polish seem small, but they form the basis for satisfying combat and gameplay. If the Anacrusis comes out of Early Access still missing even a bit of polish from its core systems, it might not be worth playing even then. 

If the game came out of EA and the zombies still had bad and boring death animations, even if they fixed everything else, improved the weight of the gunplay, improved the selection of weapons, improved zombie animations outside of that, made them more cohesive with the world and made them more fluid and less stiff, if they fixed EVERYTHING else but zombies were still unsatisfying to kill because their unblemished models still just flopped over, then the game would still suck to play. So they have a long road ahead of them getting ALL of this stuff polished.

I hope they can pull it off.
It's L4D in a 70's theme space station. The AI director is good. I shoot the enemies.
